alpha.selection_rationale: Five stacked torpedo cruisers spend 150 exactly, share 1.5g so nothing is abandoned, and dump coordinated 40-round waves that the catalog itself says will overwhelm even dreadnought PD. Simple order: stay nose-on as a brick, close, and salvo together — empty gunships and slow capitals die; a pure kite is the only real threat and cannot spend this budget at 3g under the 8-ship cap.
alpha.formation_rationale: Identical torpedo cruisers held well aft so fragile hulls stay out of early gun range and can fire a coordinated volley. Center-plus-tetrahedron keeps every pair ~43–71 km apart for full mutual PD overlap while modest 3-axis offsets deny a single spinal line through multiple ships.

beta.selection_rationale: Anchor the line with two dreadnoughts (0.75g) whose 251cm nose armor and 5 heavy coilguns plus spinal mount can slug it out and tank punishment, screened by five cheap frigates that add 10 extra PD lasers (crucial for shredding incoming torpedo saturation) and 5 more coilgun barrels for volume fire. All hulls stay close together in a single defensive formation rather than splitting speed doctrines, spending the full 150-point budget across 7 ships for redundancy against focused fire.
beta.formation_rationale: The two dreadnoughts form the main gunline slightly forward, close enough together (60km apart) to mass firepower while supporting each other's PD. A pair of frigates (Ward-1/2) screen ahead and to the sides of the dreadnoughts at offset altitudes to intercept torpedoes approaching the capital ships, while overlapping PD coverage. Ward-4/5 sit further out laterally to complicate the enemy's spinal weapon geometry, forcing them to choose between engaging the flanks or the core, while still within PD-support range (~100km) of the dreadnoughts. Ward-3 is held in reserve at the rear, away from the initial exchange, ready to reinforce PD or respond to flanking maneuvers without being an easy target in the opening exchange.
